invalid.claim: A thinks B's shopping list is complete (covers everything B needs)

decisions.reason: Turn 5 'Is that on your list?' uses definite possessive 'your list' presupposing B has a shopping list. Turn 3 'Have you written down...' also presupposes B is maintaining a list.

decisions.claim: B is going shopping with A
decisions.reason: Turn 1 'Are you ready to go shopping?' presupposes B is going shopping. Turn 9 'Have we got enough money?' uses 'we' confirming joint activity with A.

decisions.claim: B may have written down potatoes, carrots, and onions on the list
decisions.reason: Turn 3 is a question asking whether B wrote items down. Questions do not establish their answers. The 'may have' hedge makes this speculative rather than a grounded attribute.
decisions.counterexample: B may not have written anything down; A is simply asking.

decisions.claim: B proposed an idea that A approved
decisions.reason: Turn 3 'Good idea.' is A's response to something B proposed, presupposing B made a suggestion that A approved.

decisions.claim: B mentioned two options that A decided to get both of
decisions.reason: Turn 5 'Let's get both' presupposes B mentioned two options and A decided to get both. The word 'both' requires a prior mention of two items by B.

decisions.claim: B is expected to drive or has been driving
decisions.reason: Turn 11 'Shall I drive?' is A offering to drive. It does not presuppose B is expected to drive or has been driving; A is volunteering. The question 'Shall I drive?' actually suggests A is offering, not that B was expected to.
decisions.counterexample: B may not drive at all; A is offering to drive instead.

decisions.claim: B asked A something that A responded to with uncertainty
decisions.reason: Turn 9 'I'm not sure.' is A's response to a question B asked (likely about cheese or money). This presupposes B asked something that A answered with uncertainty.
